title: Opaque KV-cache TTL mismatch leads to cross-namespace read exposure under Dedicated failover
creator: Avery Chen
description: Several Dedicated customers reported intermittent 403/200 anomalies after a regional failover. Investigation shows the shared opaque KV cache used to accelerate API-key/org resolution had a TTL mismatch between read-path and write-path code paths during edge failover and leader elections. This allowed stale (but valid) KV entries scoped to one org to be returned for requests routed to a different tenant under certain timing windows, effectively exposing brief read access to metadata (org id, role flags, routing hints) for the wrong namespace.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Provision 2 dedicated nodes in region A (primary) and region B (hot spare).
2) Create two test customers (org-A and org-B) with distinct API keys and short-lived session metadata writes to the KV cache (TTL 30s).
3) Generate sustained traffic to primary with frequent token refresh and small writes to per-request cache hints.
4) Trigger a simulated failover by killing the primary node and shifting traffic to region B while simultaneously replaying some cached responses via a stale edge connection.
5) Observe that under a narrow timing window (~200-800ms) a request authenticated for org-B receives org-A metadata in server logs and returns a 200 for a metadata fetch that should have been 403.
6) Reproduce more reliably by increasing KV write latency and injecting leader election jitter (use local test harness scripts).
investigation_notes: Initial support signal: SE escalations from 2 enterprise customers with Dedicated clusters; they reported sensitive metadata mismatches but no PII exfiltration confirmed.
Logs correlated to instance IDs show cache-get paths did not verify namespace binding atomically when cache entries were created during leader transition.

Race is between async cache invalidation job (on failover) and a fallback read-path that tries stale fallback entries; write path sets TTL as integer seconds, read path used milliseconds-based expiry comparison in one compiled runtime (arm64 optimized build).

Root cause: inconsistent expiry unit (s vs ms) introduced in kvcache shim during a perf PR that targeted ARM builds. The mismatch increases perceived TTL by ~1000x on some nodes, leaving stale entries alive through failover windows.
Reproducible in staging with musl/arm64 image used by edge nodes; not triggered in standard amd64 tests which masked the unit mismatch.
Risk: metadata fields exposed are non-sensitive routing flags and org ids. No user content or secret keys observed in logs. Still high-severity due to cross-tenant leakage vector.
Customer communications: SEs sent interim notice describing mitigation steps and that investigation is prioritized P0. Legal and security notified; prepared for disclosure if needed.
mitigation_actions: Hotfix rollout: disable edge-level stale-read fallback path via feature flag (edge.disable_stale_fallback=true) — immediate mitigation for affected Dedicated clusters.
Invalidate kvcache on leader transition more aggressively: trigger synchronous invalidate for entries created in last 60s for now.
Scoped rollback: revert ARM-specific perf PR that introduced milliseconds->seconds mismatch from 2026-02-28 build in affected node images.
Customer assist: SEs will run invalidate script and toggle feature flag in customer-managed planes where we have access, coordinate maintenance windows for those that require action.
proposed_fix: 1) Normalize expiry units across all kvcache code paths (force use of nanoseconds via monotonic clock wrappers).
2) Add namespace binding verification to cache-get path: returned entry must include canonical org hash and request must match or entry is rejected.
3) Add invariant unit tests covering arm64/amd64 builds and a dedicated CI job that runs leader-election/failover scenarios with the kvcache harness.
4) Backport hotfix and patch release to runtime-1.24 and create a dedicated image tag for affected Dedicated customers (runtime-1.24.1-dedicated-hotfix).
5) Add a telemetry event for 'cache_namespace_mismatch' and a rate-limited alert to PagerDuty.
qa_plan: Add end-to-end scenario in staging with synthetic failover harness validating no cross-namespace metadata reads after failover (1000 iterations).
Run chaos tests with randomized clock skew in CI and verify expiry behavior remains consistent.
Smoke test template for SEs: run kvcache-invalidate and verify customer test keys return correct namespace within 60s.
Security-run: threat model review for kvcache flows and confirm no persisted historical exposures.
follow_up_tasks: Postmortem draft with timeline, RCA, and compensating controls (owner: Avery Chen).
Instrument audit logs to capture cache-hit metadata bundle for 90 days (owner: Platform Observability).
Customer outreach plan and compliance sign-off for each impacted account (owner: CSM).
Policy: add a build-time lint to prevent unit-inconsistent time math across languages (owner: Infra Eng).
Schedule retro to tighten Dedicated failover playbooks and SE runbooks (owner: Reliability PM).
